SIKADUR®-41 CF NORMAL: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikadur®-41 CF Normal, November 2023, Version 01.03 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/p/sikadur-41-cf-normal.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikadur®-41 CF Normal where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (November 2023, Version 01.03).
1.2 Product description. Sikadur®-41 CF Normal is a 3-component thixotropic mortar based on epoxy resin and selected aggregates. Sikadur®-41 CF Normal is made up of Sikadur-31 Part A and B and Sikadur Aggregates 501. The fully cured mortar exhibits physical and mechanical properties. Sikadur®-41 CF Normal is easy to apply and is ideally suited to site application.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. As a repair and bonding mortar for:
    - Concrete elements
    - Hard natural stone
    - Ceramics, fibre cement
    - Mortar, Bricks, Masonry
    - Steel, Iron, Aluminium
    - Wood
    - Polyester, Epoxy
    - Glass
1.4 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - As a repair mortar.
    - Filling of cavities and voids
    - Vertical and overhead use
    - Corners and edges
    - Joint and crack arris / edge repair
    As an abrasion and impact resistant wearing course:
1.5 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.7.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikadur®-41 CF Normal
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: HIGH STRENGTH EPOXY RESIN PATCHING MORTAR
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Certificates and test reports. Mortar for structural and non-structural repair, tested according to EN 1504-3, provided with the CE-mark
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 1504-3: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - DIN EN 196: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Compressive strength (p.2); Technical Information > Flexural-strength (p.2).
    - ASTM D 695: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Modulus of elasticity in compression (p.2).
    - ISO 527: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Modulus of elasticity in tension (p.2); Technical Information > Tensile strain at break (p.2); Technical Information > Tensile strength (p.2).
    - EN ISO 4624: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN 12188: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN 1770: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Coefficient of thermal expansion (p.2).
    - EN 1799: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Sag flow (p.2).
    - EN ISO 9514: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Pot Life (p.3).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer. Sikadur®-41 CF Normal has the following advantages:
    - Easy to mix and apply
    - Very good adhesion to most construction materials
    - High strength
    - Thixotropic: Non-sag in vertical and overhead applications
    - Hardens without shrinkage
    - Different coloured components (for mixing control)
    - No primer needed
    - High initial and ultimate mechanical strength
    - Good abrasion resistance
    - Good chemical resistance
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Epoxy resin
    - Colour: Component A: white; Component B: dark grey; Component C: sand; Components A+B+C mixed: concrete grey
    - Density: 1.98 ± 0.1 kg/l (component A+B+C mixed) (at +21 °C)
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Modulus of elasticity in compression: ~ 9,000 N/mm² (14 days at +23 °C) (ASTM D 695)
    - Modulus of elasticity in tension: ~ 4,000 N/mm²(14 days at +23 °C) (ISO 527)
    - Tensile strain at break: 0.2 ± 0.1 % (7 days at +23 °C) (ISO 527)
    - Shrinkage: Hardens without shrinkage.
    - Coefficient of thermal expansion: 3.5 x 10⁻⁵ 1/K (Temp. range +23 °C − +60 °C) (EN 1770)
2.7 Compressive strength.
    | Curing time | Curing temperature |
    | +10 °C | +23 °C | +30 °C |
    | 1 day | ~18 N/mm² | ~62 N/mm² | ~72 N/mm² |
    | 3 days | ~50 N/mm² | ~79 N/mm² | ~81 N/mm² |
    | 7 days | ~64 N/mm² | ~82 N/mm² | ~82 N/mm² |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (DIN EN 196)
2.8 Flexural-strength.

    | 7 days | ~31 N/mm² | ~38 N/mm² | ~38 N/mm² |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (DIN EN 196)
2.9 Tensile strength.

2.11 Heat deflection temperature.

    Test method printed: (ISO 75)
    Note printed: (thickness 10 mm)
2.12 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 11 kg, net pre-proportioned kits. Sikadur®-41 CF Normal consists of Sikadur-31 Parts A and B, plus Sikadur Aggregates 501.
    - Shelf life: 24 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: Store in original, unopened, sealed and undamaged packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +30 °C. Protect from direct sunlight.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (November 2023, Version 01.03) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality. Mortar and concrete must be older than 28 days (depends on minimal requirement of strengths). Verify the substrate strength (concrete, masonry, natural stone). The substrate surface (all types) must be clean, dry or mat damp (no standing water) and free from contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, existing surface treatments and coatings etc. Steel substrates must be de-rusted similar to Sa 2.5 The substrate must be sound and all loose particles must be removed.
3.3 Substrate preparation - Concrete, mortar, stone, bricks. Substrates must be sound, dry or mat damp (no standing water) , clean and free from laitance, ice, grease, oils, old surface treatments or coatings and all loose or friable particles must be removed to achieve a laitance and contaminant free, open textured surface.
3.4 Substrate preparation - Steel. Must be cleaned and prepared thoroughly to an acceptable quality i.e. by blast-cleaning and vacuum. Avoid dew point conditions.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (November 2023, Version 01.03) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: Component A : B : C = 2 : 1 : 2.5 by weight; Component A : B : C = 2 : 1 : 3.4 by volume
    - Consumption: The consumption of Sikadur®-41 CF Normal is ~ 2.0 kg/m² per mm of thickness.
    - Layer thickness: 3 mm min. / 60 mm max.
    - Sag flow: On vertical surfaces it is non-sag up to 20 mm thickness. (EN 1799)
4.3 Pot Life.
    | Temperature | Pot life* | Open time |
    | +10 °C | ~ 180 minutes |
    | +23 °C | ~ 60 minutes |
    | +30 °C | ~ 40 minutes | ~ 50 minutes |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (EN ISO 9514)
    Note printed: *200 g The pot life begins when the resin and hardener are mixed. It is shorter at high temperatures and longer at low temperatures. The larger the quantity mixed, the shorter the pot life. To obtain longer workability at high temperatures, the mixed adhesive may be divided into portions. Another method is to chill components A+B before mixing them (not below +5 °C).
4.4 Mixing - Pre-batched units. Mix components A+B together for at least 3 minutes with a mixing spindle attached to a slow speed electric drill (max. 300 rpm) until the material becomes smooth in consistency and a uniform grey colour. Then add part C and continue until mixture is homogeneous. Avoid aeration while mixing. Then, pour the whole mix into a clean container and stir again for approx. 1 more minute at low speed to keep air entrapment at a minimum. Mix only that quantity which can be used within its pot life.
4.5 Application method / tools.
    - Brush the adhesive well into the substrate. Sikadur®-31 CF can be used as primer to improve the bond.
    - When using a thin layer adhesive, apply the mixed adhesive to the prepared surface with a spatula, trowel, notched trowel, (or with hands protected by gloves). When applying as a repair mortar, use some formwork.
    - When using for bonding metal profiles onto vertical surfaces ,support and press uniformly using props for at least 12 hours, depending on the thickness applied (not more than 5 mm) and the room temperature. Once hardened check the adhesion by tapping with a hammer.
4.6 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with Sika® Colma Cleaner immediately after use. Hardened / cured material can only be removed mechanically.
4.7 Limitations and important considerations. Sikadur® resins are formulated to have low creep under permanent loading. However due to the creep behaviour of all polymer materials under load, the long term structural design load must account for creep. Generally the long term structural design load must be lower than 20–25 % of the failure load.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Material temperature. Sikadur®-41 CF Normal must be applied at a temperatures between +10 °C and +30 °C.
5.3 Ambient air temperature. +10 °C min. / +30 °C max.
5.4 Dew point. Beware of condensation. Substrate temperature during application must be at least 3 °C above dew point.
5.5 Substrate temperature. +10 °C min. / +30 °C max.
5.6 Substrate moisture content. Substrate must be dry or mat damp (no standing water); Brush the adhesive well into the substrate
5.7 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Compressive strength: Curing time | Curing temperature; +10 °C | +23 °C | +30 °C; 1 day | ~18 N/mm² | ~62 N/mm² | ~72 N/mm²; 3 days | ~50 N/mm² | ~79 N/mm² | ~81 N/mm²; 7 days | ~64 N/mm² | ~82 N/mm² | ~82 N/mm² (DIN EN 196)
    - Modulus of elasticity in compression: ~ 9,000 N/mm² (14 days at +23 °C) (ASTM D 695)
    - Flexural-strength: Curing time | Curing temperature; +10 °C | +23 °C | +30 °C; 1 day | ~9 N/mm² | ~22 N/mm² | ~25 N/mm²; 3 days | ~19 N/mm² | ~26 N/mm² | ~30 N/mm²; 7 days | ~31 N/mm² | ~38 N/mm² | ~38 N/mm² (DIN EN 196)
    - Tensile strength: Curing time | Curing temperature; +25 °C | +35 °C | +45 °C; 1 day | ~4 N/mm² | ~15 N/mm² | ~17 N/mm²; 3 days | ~15 N/mm² | ~17 N/mm² | ~19 N/mm²; 7 days | ~16 N/mm² | ~19 N/mm² | ~21 N/mm² (ISO 527)
    - Modulus of elasticity in tension: ~ 4,000 N/mm²(14 days at +23 °C) (ISO 527)
    - Tensile strain at break: 0.2 ± 0.1 % (7 days at +23 °C) (ISO 527)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: Curing time | Substrate | Curing tem- | Adhesion; perature | strength; 7 days | Concrete dry | +10 °C | > 4 N/mm² *; 7 days | Concrete | +10 °C | > 4 N/mm² *; moist; 7 days | Steel | +10 °C | ~6 N/mm²; 7 days | Steel | +23 °C | ~15 N/mm² (EN ISO 4624, EN 1542, EN 12188)
    - Coefficient of thermal expansion: 3.5 x 10⁻⁵ 1/K (Temp. range +23 °C − +60 °C) (EN 1770)
    - Heat deflection temperature: Curing time | Curing temperat- | HDT; ure; 7 days | +23 °C | +49 °C (ISO 75)
    - Sag flow: On vertical surfaces it is non-sag up to 20 mm thickness. (EN 1799)
    - Pot Life: Temperature | Pot life* | Open time; +10 °C | ~ 180 minutes; +23 °C | ~ 60 minutes; +30 °C | ~ 40 minutes | ~ 50 minutes (EN ISO 9514)
5.8 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.9 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikadur®-41 CF Normal, November 2023, Version 01.03, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/p/sikadur-41-cf-normal.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikadur-41 CF Normal (B), version 24/10/2023, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/a/MSDS%20Sikadur-41%20CF%20Normal%20(B)%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikadur-41 CF Normal (A), version 24/10/2023, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/g/MSDS%20Sikadur-41%20CF%20Normal%20(A)%20GHS7.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
